To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AAFBR is a robust Bayes factor that can be used to quantify support in the data for informative hypotheses regarding group means in the case of non normality or outlier presence.
the AAFBRob is a robust alternative to the AAFB.
the AAFBFRob is less affected by non normal distributions and outliers and that the AABFRob is therefore preferred over the AABF in the presence of non normality or the presence of outliers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of the robust Bayes Factor AAFBFROb.
the use of the AABF in a Bayesian ANOVA setting and the effect of nonnormality and outliers on the AAFBF.
the development of the robust Bayes factors AAFBFROBs for the evaluation of informative hypotheses with regards of group means in Bayesian ANOVAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AAFBR is a useful tool for researchers to evaluate pairs of informative hypotheses, but the AAFBF should not be used when non normality and/or outliers are present in the data.
the use of the AABBFROB is strongly recommended when the sample sizes are small and the data are non normal.
the AAFBRROB can be seen as a valuable addition to the AAFBF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robust Bayesian ANOVA is a useful alternative for the classical Bayesian ANOVA in situations with non-normality and/or outliers.
the robust Bayes Factor AAFBFROBs is recommended for use when non normality and/or outliers are suspected to be present in the data.
the AAFBRobust is a useful tool in Bayesian ANOVA when the sample mean and sample variance estimates are not robust against non normality and/or outliers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers should be aware of the fact that non normality and outlier can have a negative impact on the AAFBF.
the AAFBRROB is recommended when there is a risk that the data are not normal.
